Project Guidelines and Standards: herdr

This document defines the guidelines and best practices for developing the herdr package in collaboration with Antigravity and AI coding assistants.

1. Project Overview

  • Package: herdr
  • Type: R Package (>= 4.1.0) with Shiny GUI support (run_app()).
  • Domain: Livestock greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and feed-related land use footprint accounting based on IPCC Tier 2 methodologies and nutritional guidelines (ruminants and monogastrics).
  • Core Branches:
    • main: Production-ready, stable releases.
    • dev: Active integration and daily development branch.

2. R Coding Standards

  1. Code Style:
    • Follow the Tidyverse style guide (styler / lintr).
    • Use meaningful, descriptive snake_case for all function and variable names.
    • Never use library() or require() within R/ scripts. Use @importFrom package function in roxygen2 headers or explicit package::function() calls.
    • Any non-standard evaluation (NSE) column names or global symbols used in dplyr/ggplot2 pipelines must be declared in R/globals.R via utils::globalVariables() to prevent R CMD check notes.
  2. Documentation (roxygen2):
    • All exported functions must have complete roxygen2 documentation blocks including:
      • Clear @title and @description.
      • Explicit @param descriptions with data types and physical units (e.g., kg CH4/head/year, MJ/day).
      • Concrete @return defining output data types and structures.
      • @export only for public-facing API functions.
      • Reproducible @examples (wrap in \dontrun{} if requiring heavy external data downloads).
  3. Methodological & Mathematical Rigor:
    • Calculations must strictly adhere to IPCC guidelines (2006 / 2019 Refinement) and referenced animal nutrition literature.
    • Document specific equations in source code comments (e.g., # IPCC 2019, Vol 4, Ch 10, Eq. 10.21).
    • Implement defensive programming and input validation using assertthat::assert_that or explicit condition checks on physical boundaries.

3. Testing and Verification (testthat)

  • Every calculation or functional module in R/ must have a corresponding test suite in tests/testthat/test_*.R.

  • Functional code must never be merged without verifying that existing and new tests pass.

  • Run tests in PowerShell via:

    & "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "pkgload::load_all('.'); testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test_NAME.R')"

  • Run the full test suite:

    & "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "pkgload::load_all('.'); devtools::test()"

  • Regenerate documentation and NAMESPACE:

    & "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "devtools::document()"

4. Git Workflow and Conventional Commits

  • Base Development Branch: dev.
  • Feature Branches: feature/<name>, fix/<name>, docs/<name>.
  • Commit Messages: Follow Conventional Commits:
    • feat(...): New feature or calculation.
    • fix(...): Bug fix or calculation correction.
    • docs(...): Documentation, pkgdown, or vignette updates.
    • test(...): Unit test additions or updates.
    • perf(...): Performance optimizations.
    • refactor(...): Code cleanup without functional changes.
  • Maintain a clean working directory (no untracked R artifacts such as .Rhistory, .RData, or .Rcheck/).
